def test_memory_set_instruction_and_overlapping_error():
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    # create a fake instruction of length 2
    inst = Instruction(opcode=0x04, operands=bytearray([0x01]), disasm_template="mov a, #IMB", addr_mode=AddressModes.ImmediateByte)
    addr = 0x0100
    mem.set_instruction(addr, inst)
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        # attempt to set overlapping instruction starting at addr+1 should raise
        inst2 = Instruction(opcode=0x05, operands=bytearray([0x02]), disasm_template="mov a, DIR", addr_mode=AddressModes.Direct)
        mem.set_instruction(addr + 1, inst2)


def test_memory_vector_set_get_and_iter():
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    addr = 0x0200
    # write two bytes representing vector target 0x1234
    mem.contents[addr] = 0x12
    mem.contents[addr + 1] = 0x34
    mem.set_vector(addr)
    assert mem.is_vector_start(addr)
    assert mem.get_vector(addr) == 0x1234
    vlist = list(mem.iter_vectors())
    assert any(vaddr == addr and target == 0x1234 for vaddr, target in vlist)


def test_memory_annotations_and_query_methods():
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    addr = 0x0300
    mem.annotate_jump_target(addr)
    mem.annotate_call_target(addr)
    mem.annotate_branch_taken(addr)
    mem.annotate_branch_not_taken(addr + 1)
    assert mem.is_jump_target(addr)
    assert mem.is_call_target(addr)
    assert mem.is_branch_taken(addr)
    assert mem.is_branch_not_taken(addr + 1)
    # mark branch always/never via the annotate methods and Tracer.annotate_branches logic
    # create an instruction at addr so annotate_branches can see it
    inst = Instruction(opcode=0x00, operands=bytearray(), disasm_template="nop", addr_mode=AddressModes.Inherent)
    mem.set_instruction(addr, inst)
    # create a tracer and run annotate_branches to produce always/never annotations
    tracer = Tracer(mem, [], [], range(0x0000, 0x10000))
    # manually annotate branch taken only at addr+2
    addr2 = addr + 2
    inst2 = Instruction(opcode=0x00, operands=bytearray(), disasm_template="nop", addr_mode=AddressModes.Inherent)
    mem.set_instruction(addr2, inst2)
    mem.annotate_branch_taken(addr2)
    tracer.annotate_branches()
    assert mem.is_branch_always_taken(addr2)


def test_sortedset_ordering_and_tracequeue_behavior():
    s = SortedSet(key=attrgetter('pc'))
    ps1 = ProcessorState(pc=0x200)
    ps2 = ProcessorState(pc=0x100)
    ps3 = ProcessorState(pc=0x300)
    s.add(ps1)
    s.add(ps2)
    s.add(ps3)
    # pop should return in sorted order by pc (100,200,300)
    popped = [s.pop(), s.pop(), s.pop()]
    assert [p.pc for p in popped] == [0x100, 0x200, 0x300]
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        s.pop()

    tq = TraceQueue()
    # push a processor state twice -> only stored once
    tq.push(ps1)
    tq.push(ps1)
    assert len(tq.untraced_processor_states) == 1
    popped_ps = tq.pop()
    assert isinstance(popped_ps, ProcessorState)
    # traced_processor_states contains it; pushing again should be ignored
    tq.push(popped_ps)
    assert len(tq.untraced_processor_states) == 0


def test_tracer_enqueue_vector_and_trace_marks_instruction_and_data():
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    # create a vector at 0x0100 pointing to 0x0110
    vec_addr = 0x0100
    target = 0x0110
    mem.contents[vec_addr] = (target >> 8) & 0xFF
    mem.contents[vec_addr + 1] = target & 0xFF
    # place a nop at the target
    mem.contents[target] = 0x00
    trace_range = range(0x0100, 0x0200)
    tracer = Tracer(mem, [], [vec_addr], trace_range)
    tracer.trace(disassemble_inst)
    # vector should be recorded
    assert mem.is_vector_start(vec_addr)
    # the target instruction should have been disassembled and stored
    assert mem.is_instruction_start(target)
    # locations in the traceable range not marked as instruction should be data
    some_addr = 0x0150
    assert mem.is_data(some_addr)


def test_tracer_annotate_branches_sets_always_and_never():
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    tracer = Tracer(mem, [], [], range(0x0000, 0x10000))
    addr = 0x0100
    # create an instruction so iter_instructions yields it
    inst = Instruction(opcode=0xFC, operands=bytearray([0x00]), disasm_template="bne REL", addr_mode=AddressModes.Relative)
    mem.set_instruction(addr, inst)
    # annotate branch taken only
    mem.annotate_branch_taken(addr)
    tracer.annotate_branches()
    assert mem.is_branch_always_taken(addr)
    # now annotate not taken only for a different addr
    addr2 = 0x0200
    inst2 = Instruction(opcode=0xFD, operands=bytearray([0x00]), disasm_template="beq REL", addr_mode=AddressModes.Relative)
    mem.set_instruction(addr2, inst2)
    mem.annotations[addr2].clear()
    mem.annotate_branch_not_taken(addr2)
    tracer.annotate_branches()
    assert mem.is_branch_never_taken(addr2)


def test_symbol_table_generates_code_and_data_symbols():
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    start_address = 0x0100
    symtab = SymbolTable({})
    # mark a call target address and provide an instruction start there
    call_addr = 0x0120
    inst_call = Instruction(opcode=0x31, operands=bytearray([0x01, 0x20]), disasm_template="call EXT", addr_mode=AddressModes.Extended)
    mem.set_instruction(call_addr, inst_call)
    mem.annotate_call_target(call_addr)
    symtab.generate_code_symbols(mem, start_address)
    assert call_addr in symtab.symbols
    name, _ = symtab.symbols[call_addr]
    assert name.startswith("sub_")

    # generate data symbol for direct addressing reference
    ref_addr = 0x0130
    inst_ref_loc = 0x0110
    inst_ref = Instruction(opcode=0x05, operands=bytearray([ref_addr & 0xFF]), disasm_template="mov a, DIR", addr_mode=AddressModes.Direct)
    mem.set_instruction(inst_ref_loc, inst_ref)
    # ensure ref_addr is start of single/multibyte (it is Unknown so it's start)
    symtab.generate_data_symbols(mem, start_address)
    assert ref_addr in symtab.symbols
    name2, _ = symtab.symbols[ref_addr]
    assert name2.startswith("mem_")

    # immediate word stored into pointer produces symbol
    store_addr = 0x0140
    inst_store_loc = 0x0112
    inst_store = Instruction(opcode=0xE7, operands=bytearray([0x01, 0x40]), disasm_template="movw ep, #IMW", addr_mode=AddressModes.ImmediateWord)
    mem.set_instruction(inst_store_loc, inst_store)
    symtab.generate_data_symbols(mem, start_address)
    assert store_addr in symtab.symbols


def test_printer_format_and_print_lines(capsys):
    mem = make_empty_memory()
    start_address = 0x0100
    # prepare a small symbol table
    symtab = SymbolTable({0x00: ("pdr0", "port 0 data register")})
    printer = Printer(mem, start_address, symtab)

    # test header printing
    printer.print_header()
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert ".F2MC8L" in captured.out
    assert ".org" in captured.out

    # test format_ext_address and format_dir_address using symbols and numeric fallback
    assert printer.format_ext_address(0x00) == "pdr0"
    assert "0x%04x" % 0x1234 == printer.format_ext_address(0x1234)
    assert printer.format_dir_address(0x00) == "pdr0"
    assert "0x%02x" % 0x12 == printer.format_dir_address(0x12)

    # test printing vector line
    vec_addr = 0x0200
    target = 0x0301
    mem.contents[vec_addr] = (target >> 8) & 0xFF
    mem.contents[vec_addr + 1] = target & 0xFF
    mem.set_vector(vec_addr)
    printer.print_vector_line(vec_addr)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert ".word" in out
    assert "VECTOR" in out

    # test mode and reserved byte lines
    mb_addr = 0x0400
    mem.contents[mb_addr] = 0xAB
    mem.set_mode_byte(mb_addr)
    printer.print_mode_byte_line(mb_addr)
    rb_addr = 0x0401
    mem.contents[rb_addr] = 0xCD
    mem.set_reserved_byte(rb_addr)
    printer.print_reserved_byte_line(rb_addr)
    out2 = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "MODE" in out2
    assert "RESERVED" in out2

    # test data line printing
    data_addr = 0x0500
    mem.contents[data_addr] = 0x41  # ASCII 'A'
    mem.set_data(data_addr)
    printer.print_data_line(data_addr)
    out3 = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert ".byte" in out3
    assert "DATA" in out3

    # test instruction line printing including .byte path for extended page0
    # create an extended instruction with address in page 0
    inst_addr = 0x0600
    target_ext = 0x0033  # page 0
    # pick an extended opcode that is not excluded (e.g., 0x60 mov a, EXT)
    mem.contents[inst_addr] = 0x60
    mem.contents[inst_addr + 1] = (target_ext >> 8) & 0xFF
    mem.contents[inst_addr + 2] = target_ext & 0xFF

    mem.set_instruction(pc, inst_nop)
    printer.print_instruction_line(pc, inst_nop)
    out5 = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "nop" in out5.lower()

    class BadMemory:

def test_compute_blast_radius_and_enrich():
    # Graph A with chain D->C->B->A
    nodes = [{"id": n} for n in ("a.py", "b.py", "c.py", "d.py")]
    links = [
        {"source": "b.py", "target": "a.py"},
        {"source": "c.py", "target": "b.py"},
        {"source": "d.py", "target": "c.py"},
    ]

    assert a["transitive_dependents"] == 2
    # enrich nodes
    enriched = impact_mod.enrich_nodes(nodes, blast)
    assert all("blast_score" in n for n in enriched)
    # enrich links imports/imported_by

    nid_map = {n["id"]: n for n in enriched_nodes}
    assert "b.py" in nid_map["d.py"]["imports"] or isinstance(nid_map["d.py"]["imports"], list)

def make_jwt(header: dict, payload: dict, corrupt_payload=False):
    def b64url(data: bytes) -> str:
        s = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).decode().rstrip("=")
        return s
    header_b = b64url(json.dumps(header).encode())
    if corrupt_payload:
        payload_b = "!!notbase64!!"
    else:
        payload_b = b64url(json.dumps(payload).encode())
    sig = "sig"  # dummy
    return f"{header_b}.{payload_b}.{sig}"

    ]

        {"source": "B", "target": "C"},

    ]

    assert blast["A"]["direct_dependents"] == 0
    # Enrich nodes

    assert any(n.get("blast_score") is not None for n in enriched_nodes)
    # Enrich links (imports/imported_by)
    enriched_nodes = enrich_links(enriched_nodes, links)
    a = next(n for n in enriched_nodes if n["id"] == "A")
    # A should import B and D
    assert "B" in a["imports"] and "D" in a["imports"]
    # Reporter strings contain expected substrings
    out = reporter.format_stdout("A", blast["A"], total_nodes=4)
    assert "Blast Score" in out
    md = reporter.format_markdown("A", blast["A"], total_nodes=4)

def make_memory_zeroed():
    # Memory with empty ROM produces 0x10000 zeros
    return Memory(b'')


def write_bytes(mem, address, data):
    for i, b in enumerate(data):
        mem.contents[(address + i) & 0xFFFF] = b


def test_disassemble_immediate_byte_and_str():
    mem = make_memory_zeroed()
    pc = 0x0100
    write_bytes(mem, pc, b'\x04\xAA')  # mov a, #0xaa
    inst = disassemble_inst(mem, pc)
    assert inst.opcode == 0x04
    assert inst.immediate == 0xAA
    assert len(inst) == 2
    s = str(inst)
    assert "mov a" in s
    assert "0xaa" in s  # formatted lowercase as per Instruction.__str__


def test_disassemble_extended_and_vector_resolution():
    mem = make_memory_zeroed()
    # Extended call: 0x31 aa bb -> address 0xaabb
    pc_ext = 0x0200
    write_bytes(mem, pc_ext, b'\x31\x12\x34')
    inst_ext = disassemble_inst(mem, pc_ext)
    assert inst_ext.addr_mode == AddressModes.Extended
    assert inst_ext.address == 0x1234

    # Vector call: opcode 0xe8..0xef map to vectors at 0xffc0 + (callv*2)
    pc_vec = 0x0300
    # Setup vector for callv #2 -> vector address 0xffc0 + 4 = 0xffc4
    vec_index = 2
    vec_addr = 0xffc0 + vec_index * 2
    # Put target 0x4567 into that vector
    mem.contents[vec_addr] = 0x45
    mem.contents[(vec_addr + 1) & 0xFFFF] = 0x67
    # Place opcode e8 + vec_index (vector addressing)
    write_bytes(mem, pc_vec, bytes([0xe8 + vec_index]))
    inst_vec = disassemble_inst(mem, pc_vec)
    assert inst_vec.addr_mode == AddressModes.Vector
    assert inst_vec.callv == vec_index
    # should resolve to 0x4567
    assert inst_vec.address == 0x4567


def test_disassemble_relative_positive_and_negative():
    mem = make_memory_zeroed()
    # positive displacement: beq REL (0xfd) with displacement 0x05
    pc = 0x1000
    write_bytes(mem, pc, b'\xfd\x05')
    inst = disassemble_inst(mem, pc)
    assert inst.addr_mode == AddressModes.Relative
    # disassembly resolves relative to pc + instlen (instlen==2 for relative)
    expected = (pc + 2 + 0x05) & 0xFFFF
    assert inst.address == expected

    # negative displacement example: displacement 0xFB => -5
    pc2 = 0x2000
    write_bytes(mem, pc2, b'\xfd\xfb')
    inst2 = disassemble_inst(mem, pc2)
    expected2 = (pc2 + 2 - 5) & 0xFFFF
    assert inst2.address == expected2


def test_disassemble_bitdirect_with_relative():
    mem = make_memory_zeroed()
    pc = 0x1100
    # bbc DIR:BIT, REL -> opcode 0xb3 (bit = 0xb3 & 7 = 3)
    write_bytes(mem, pc, b'\xb3\xAA\x05')
    inst = disassemble_inst(mem, pc)
    assert inst.addr_mode == AddressModes.BitDirectWithRelative
    assert inst.bit == (0xb3 & 0b111)
    assert inst.bit == 3
    assert inst.bittest_address == 0xAA
    # REL resolved relative to pc + instlen (instlen==3 here)
    assert inst.address == ((pc + 3 + 0x05) & 0xFFFF)

def _b64url_encode(data: bytes) -> str:
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(data).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii")


def make_jwt(header: dict, payload: dict, signature: bytes = b"sig") -> str:
    return f"{_b64url_encode(json.dumps(header).encode())}.{_b64url_encode(json.dumps(payload).encode())}.{_b64url_encode(signature)}"

def test_set_and_reset_request_token_and_bearer_credential():
    # Ensure no token initially
    token_target = auth_context.TokenTarget.KUSTO
    # Set token
    ctx = auth_context.set_request_token(token_target, "abc123")
    try:
        cred = auth_context.BearerTokenCredential(token_target)
        at = cred.get_token("scope")
        assert hasattr(at, "token") and at.token == "abc123"
    finally:
        # Reset
        auth_context.reset_request_token(ctx)

    # After reset, getting token should raise
    cred2 = auth_context.BearerTokenCredential(token_target)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        cred2.get_token("scope")

def test_decode_base64url_padding_and_invalid():
    # Prepare base64url without padding
    payload = {"a": 1}
    enc = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(payload).encode()).decode()
    # convert to base64url and strip padding
    enc_url = enc.replace("+", "-").replace("/", "_").rstrip("=")
    decoded = auth_middleware._decode_base64url(enc_url)
    assert json.loads(decoded) == payload

    # Invalid characters cause exception
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        auth_middleware._decode_base64url("###invalid###")


def make_jwt(header: dict, payload: dict, signature: str = "sig"):
    def b64url(obj):
        s = base64.b64encode(json.dumps(obj).encode()).decode().replace("+", "-").replace("/", "_").rstrip("=")
        return s

    return f"{b64url(header)}.{b64url(payload)}.{base64.b64encode(signature.encode()).decode().replace('+','-').replace('/','_').rstrip('=')}"


def test_decode_jwt_token_and_validation():
    # Valid JWT
    jwt = make_jwt({"alg": "RS256"}, {"exp": int((asyncio.get_event_loop().time() + 3600))})
    payload = auth_middleware.decode_jwt_token(jwt)
    assert isinstance(payload, dict)

    # Malformed token parts
    assert auth_middleware.decode_jwt_token("a.b") == {}

    # Payload not JSON
    header = base64.b64encode(json.dumps({"alg": "RS256"}).encode()).decode().replace("+", "-").replace("/", "_").rstrip("=")
    bad_payload = base64.b64encode(b"not-json").decode().replace("+", "-").replace("/", "_").rstrip("=")
    token = f"{header}.{bad_payload}.sig"
    assert auth_middleware.decode_jwt_token(token) == {}


def test_validate_jwt_token_format_and_structure_and_expiration():
    good = make_jwt({"alg": "RS256"}, {"exp": int(asyncio.get_event_loop().time() + 3600)})
    ok, msg = auth_middleware.validate_jwt_token_format(good)
    assert ok

    bad = "a.b"
    ok2, msg2 = auth_middleware.validate_jwt_token_format(bad)
    assert not ok2

    # Structure: unsupported alg
    token_bad_alg = make_jwt({"alg": "HS256"}, {"exp": int(asyncio.get_event_loop().time() + 3600)})
    ok3, msg3 = auth_middleware.validate_jwt_token_structure(token_bad_alg)
    assert not ok3 and "unsupported algorithm" in msg3.lower()

    # Missing alg
    token_no_alg = make_jwt({}, {"exp": int(asyncio.get_event_loop().time() + 3600)})
    ok4, msg4 = auth_middleware.validate_jwt_token_structure(token_no_alg)
    assert not ok4

    # Expiration: no exp claim is valid
    ok5, _ = auth_middleware.validate_jwt_token_expiration({})
    assert ok5

    # Expired
    ok6, _ = auth_middleware.validate_jwt_token_expiration({"exp": 0})
    assert not ok6


def test_validate_token_composition():
    # Invalid format
    ok, msg = auth_middleware.validate_token("a.b")
    assert not ok

    # Bad structure alg
    tok = make_jwt({"alg": "HS256"}, {})
    ok2, msg2 = auth_middleware.validate_token(tok)
    assert not ok2

    # Expired payload
    expired = make_jwt({"alg": "RS256"}, {"exp": 0})
    ok3, _ = auth_middleware.validate_token(expired)
    assert not ok3

    # Valid token
    valid = make_jwt({"alg": "RS256"}, {"exp": int(asyncio.get_event_loop().time() + 3600)}, signature="sig")
    ok4, _ = auth_middleware.validate_token(valid)
    assert ok4


def test_tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload_and_token_target_mapping():
    # Not an object
    assert auth_middleware._tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload("not-a-dict") is None

    # Wrong method
    payload = {"method": "something/else", "params": {"name": "x"}}
    assert auth_middleware._tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload(payload) is None

    # Missing params
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        auth_middleware._tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload({"method": "tools/call"})

    # params not dict
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        auth_middleware._tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload({"method": "tools/call", "params": "no-dict"})

    # Missing name
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        auth_middleware._tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload({"method": "tools/call", "params": {}})

    # Proper mapping
    payload2 = {"method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "kusto_query"}}
    assert auth_middleware._tool_name_from_jsonrpc_payload(payload2) == "kusto_query"
    assert auth_middleware.token_target_for_tool_name("kusto_query") == auth_context.TokenTarget.KUSTO
    assert auth_middleware.token_target_for_tool_name("map_create") == auth_context.TokenTarget.FABRIC

def test_token_obo_exchanger_success_and_failure(monkeypatch):
    # Ensure obo_config allowed audiences include our resource
    monkeypatch.setattr(token_obo_exchanger, "obo_config", config_obo.obo_config)
    ex = token_obo_exchanger.TokenOboExchanger()

    # Patch ManagedIdentityCredential to return object with get_token
    class MI:
        def __init__(self, client_id=None):
            self.client_id = client_id

        def get_token(self, scope):
            return SimpleNamespace(token="mi-assertion")

    monkeypatch.setattr(token_obo_exchanger, "ManagedIdentityCredential", MI)

    # Patch msal ConfidentialClientApplication to return object with acquire_token_on_behalf_of
    class App:
        def __init__(self, client_id=None, authority=None, client_credential=None):
            self.client_id = client_id
            self.authority = authority
            self.client_credential = client_credential

        def acquire_token_on_behalf_of(self, user_assertion=None, scopes=None):
            return {"access_token": "new-token"}

    monkeypatch.setattr(token_obo_exchanger, "msal", SimpleNamespace(ConfidentialClientApplication=App))

    token = asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(ex.perform_obo_token_exchange("user-token", config_obo.obo_config.kusto_audience))
    assert token == "new-token"

    # Failure path: acquire returns error
    class AppErr:
        def __init__(self, *a, **k):
            pass

        def acquire_token_on_behalf_of(self, user_assertion=None, scopes=None):
            return {"error": "bad", "error_description": "desc"}

    monkeypatch.setattr(token_obo_exchanger, "msal", SimpleNamespace(ConfidentialClientApplication=AppErr))
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(ex.perform_obo_token_exchange("user-token", config_obo.obo_config.kusto_audience))


def test_fabric_api_http_client_get_headers_and_request(monkeypatch):
    client = fabric_api_http_client.FabricAPIHttpClient(api_base_url="https://api.test")
    # Patch get_credential to return object with get_token returning object with token attr
    class Cred:
        def get_token(self, scope):
            return SimpleNamespace(token="fabric-token", expires_on=999999)

    monkeypatch.setattr(fabric_api_http_client, "get_credential", lambda target, authority=None: Cred())

    headers = client._get_headers({"X-Custom": "v"})
    assert headers["Authorization"] == "Bearer fabric-token"
    assert headers["X-Custom"] == "v"

    # Patch httpx.AsyncClient to simulate responses
    class FakeResponse:
        def __init__(self, status_code, text, json_obj=None):
            self.status_code = status_code
            self._text = text
            self._json = json_obj

        def json(self):
            if self._json is None:
                raise ValueError("no json")
            return self._json

        @property
        def text(self):
            return self._text

    class FakeAsyncClient:
        def __init__(self, timeout=None):
            pass

        async def __aenter__(self):
            return self

        async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
            return False

        async def get(self, url, headers=None):
            return FakeResponse(200, "ok", {"value": 1})

        async def post(self, url, json=None, headers=None):
            return FakeResponse(204, "")

        async def put(self, url, json=None, headers=None):
            return FakeResponse(200, "ok", {"result": "ok"})

        async def delete(self, url, headers=None):
            return FakeResponse(400, "bad")

    monkeypatch.setattr(fabric_api_http_client, "httpx", SimpleNamespace(AsyncClient=FakeAsyncClient))

    # Async GET
    res_get = asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(client.make_request_async("GET", "/test"))
    assert isinstance(res_get, dict)

    # Async POST -> 204 returns success dict
    res_post = asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(client.make_request_async("POST", "/test", payload={"a": 1}))
    assert res_post.get("success") is True

    # Invalid method should return error dict
    res_bad = asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(client.make_request_async("PATCH", "/test"))
    assert res_bad.get("error") is True


def test_run_async_operation_in_thread_and_direct(monkeypatch):
    client = fabric_api_http_client.FabricAPIHttpClient(api_base_url="https://api.test")

    async def coro_ok():
        return "done"

    # No running loop -> uses asyncio.run path
    res = client._run_async_operation(coro_ok())
    assert res == "done"

    # Simulate running loop by patching asyncio.get_running_loop to return an object
    class DummyLoop:
        pass

    monkeypatch.setattr(asyncio, "get_running_loop", lambda: DummyLoop())
    # This should execute the coroutine in a thread without raising
    res2 = client._run_async_operation(coro_ok())
    assert res2 == "done"
    # Restore get_running_loop by invalidating import
    importlib.reload(asyncio)


def make_kusto_result():
    class Column:
        def __init__(self, column_name):
            self.column_name = column_name

    primary = SimpleNamespace(columns=[Column("A"), Column("B")], rows=[[1, 2], [None, 4]],
                              raw_columns=[{"ColumnName": "A"}, {"ColumnName": "B"}],
                              raw_rows=[[1, 2], [None, 4]])
    return SimpleNamespace(primary_results=[primary])


def test_kusto_formatter_convert_and_parse():
    rs = make_kusto_result()
    fmt_json = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.to_json(rs)
    assert fmt_json.format == "json"
    assert isinstance(fmt_json.data, list)

    fmt_csv = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.to_csv(rs)
    assert fmt_csv.format == "csv"
    assert "A" in fmt_csv.data

    fmt_tsv = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.to_tsv(rs)
    assert fmt_tsv.format == "tsv"
    assert "A\tB" in fmt_tsv.data.splitlines()[0]

    fmt_col = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.to_columnar(rs)
    assert fmt_col.format == "columnar"
    assert "A" in fmt_col.data

    fmt_kusto = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.to_kusto_response(rs)
    assert fmt_kusto.format == "kusto_response"
    parsed = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.parse({"format": "kusto_response", "data": fmt_kusto.data})
    assert isinstance(parsed, list)

    # CSV parse roundtrip
    parsed_csv = kusto_formatter.KustoFormatter.parse({"format": "csv", "data": fmt_csv.data})
    assert isinstance(parsed_csv, list)

import struct
import pytest
from unittest import mock

from k0dasm.disassemble import (
    disassemble,
    Instruction as DisasmInstruction,
    IllegalInstructionError,
    FlowTypes,
)
from k0dasm.memory import Memory, LocationTypes, LocationAnnotations
from k0dasm.listing import Printer
from k0dasm.trace import Tracer, TraceQueue, SortedSet, ProcessorState
from k0dasm.symbols import SymbolTable


def make_mem(size=0x200):
    # helper to create a memory-like bytearray with predictable contents
    return bytearray([0x00] * size)


def test_disassemble_nop_and_len_and_str():
    mem = make_mem(4)
    mem[0] = 0x00  # nop
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.template == "nop"
    assert len(inst) == 1
    assert str(inst) == "nop"
    assert inst.flow_type == FlowTypes.Continue


def test_disassemble_movw_ax_addr16p_and_to_string():
    mem = make_mem(0x300)
    mem[0] = 0x02  # movw ax,addr16p
    mem[1] = 0x34
    mem[2] = 0x12
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.template.startswith('movw ax')
    # addr16p should be computed as 0x1234
    assert inst.addr16p == 0x1234
    s = inst.to_string()
    assert '!0x1234' in s or '0x1234' in s


def test_disassemble_callt_reads_vector_and_addr5target():
    mem = make_mem(0x500)
    # prepare vector at addr 0x40 -> 0x0200 (low, high according to code)
    # disassemble expects to read mem[addr5], mem[addr5+1] to form low, high
    mem[0x40] = 0x00  # low
    mem[0x41] = 0x02  # high
    mem[0] = 0xC1  # a byte that matches (mem[pc] & mask) == pattern for callt
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.addr5 == 0x40
    assert inst.addr5target == 0x0200
    assert inst.flow_type == FlowTypes.SubroutineCall


def test_disassemble_saddrp_illegal_raises():
    mem = make_mem(4)
    mem[0] = 0x89  # opcode that will call _saddrp on mem[1]
    # choose a low value that makes resulting saddrp odd -> triggers IllegalInstructionError
    mem[1] = 0x01
    with pytest.raises(IllegalInstructionError):
        disassemble(mem, 0)


def test_disassemble_31_opcode_illegal_byte_raises():
    mem = make_mem(8)
    mem[0] = 0x31
    # Choose a follow-up byte value that is unlikely to match any branch in 0x31 handling.
    # 0xFF probably falls through to the final else in the 0x31 handling.
    mem[1] = 0xFF
    with pytest.raises(IllegalInstructionError):
        disassemble(mem, 0)


def test_instruction_properties_and_formatting_with_symbols():
    # Create instruction with various address-like attributes
    inst = DisasmInstruction("call {addr16}", opcode=0x9a, operands=(0x00, 0x02), addr16=0x0200)
    assert len(inst) == 1 + len(inst.operands)
    assert inst.all_bytes == [inst.opcode] + list(inst.operands)
    assert inst.referenced_addresses == [0x0200]
    assert inst.target_address == 0x0200

    # Test formatting with symbols for imm16
    inst2 = DisasmInstruction("addw ax,{imm16}", opcode=0xca, operands=(0x01, 0x02), imm16=0x0200)
    symbols = {0x0200: ("symbol_here", "comment")}
    s = inst2.to_string(symbols=symbols)
    assert "symbol_here" in s

    # imm16 below 0x007f should be printed as hex, not symbol (even if present)
    inst3 = DisasmInstruction("addw ax,{imm16}", opcode=0xca, operands=(0x01,), imm16=0x0010)
    s3 = inst3.to_string(symbols={0x0010: ("should_not", "")})
    assert '0x0010' in s3


def test_memory_set_instruction_and_overwrite_error():
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 10))
    inst1 = DisasmInstruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=())
    mem.set_instruction(0x10, inst1)
    # setting an overlapping instruction should raise
    inst2 = DisasmInstruction("mov a,b", opcode=0x60, operands=(0x01,))
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        mem.set_instruction(0x11, inst2)  # 0x11 overlaps with inst1 continuation


def test_memory_vector_set_get_iter():
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 200))
    # set actual content so get_vector computes (contents[address]<<8)+contents[address+1]
    mem.contents[0x40] = 0x01
    mem.contents[0x41] = 0x02
    mem.set_vector(0x40)
    assert mem.is_vector_start(0x40)
    val = mem.get_vector(0x40)
    assert val == ((0x01 << 8) + 0x02)
    vectors = list(mem.iter_vectors(0))
    assert any(a == 0x40 for a, _ in vectors)


def test_memory_data_marking_and_queries():
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 20))
    mem.set_data(5)
    assert mem.is_data(5)
    # Unknown elsewhere
    assert mem.is_unknown(6)
    mem.annotate_entry_point(6)
    assert mem.is_entry_point(6)


def test_tracequeue_sorted_order_and_duplicates():
    tq = TraceQueue()
    ps1 = ProcessorState(pc=0x200)
    ps2 = ProcessorState(pc=0x100)
    ps3 = ProcessorState(pc=0x300)
    tq.push(ps1)
    tq.push(ps2)
    tq.push(ps3)
    # pushing duplicates should not increase queue
    tq.push(ps2)
    popped = [tq.pop().pc for _ in range(len(tq))]
    assert popped == sorted(popped)
    # traced states set should prevent re-push
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        # pop from empty queue raises
        tq.pop()


def test_sortedset_basic_behavior():
    s = SortedSet()
    s.add(3)
    s.add(1)
    s.add(2)
    assert len(s) == 3
    first = s.pop()
    assert first == 1
    assert list(s) == [2, 3]


def test_tracer_enqueue_vector_and_annotation_and_queue(tmp_path):
    # Create memory with a vector pointing to 0x80
    rom = bytearray([0x00] * 300)
    rom[0x50:0x52] = b'\x00\x02'  # not used
    mem = Memory(rom)
    tracer = Tracer(mem, entry_points=[], vectors=[], traceable_range=range(0, len(mem)))
    # write a target low/high so enqueue_vector will compute it and enqueue
    # Note: Tracer.enqueue_vector uses memory.read_word -> low at address, high at address+1 reversed compared to get_vector
    # read_word does: high = contents[address+1]; low = contents[address]; return (high<<8)+low
    # So to produce 0x0200 set contents[address]=0x00 (low), contents[address+1]=0x02 (high)
    mem.contents[0x60] = 0x00
    mem.contents[0x61] = 0x02
    tracer.enqueue_vector(0x60)
    # vector types set
    assert mem.is_vector_start(0x60)
    # target enqueued in tracer.queue
    queued = list(tracer.queue.untraced_processor_states)
    assert any(ps.pc == 0x0200 for ps in queued)


def test_tracer_trace_with_generic_handlers():
    # build a mem and a very small disassemble function to simulate flow behavior
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 0x200))

    # create a fake disassemble function that returns a conditional jump at pc 0 which branches to 0x10
    def fake_disasm(memory, pc):
        if pc == 0:
            # create an instruction that is a conditional jump to 0x10
            return DisasmInstruction("bz {reltarget}", opcode=0xad, operands=(0x10,), reltarget=0x10, flow_type=FlowTypes.ConditionalJump)
        elif pc == 1:
            # a normal continue instruction (1 byte)
            return DisasmInstruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)
        elif pc == 0x10:
            # a subroutine call to 0x20
            return DisasmInstruction("call {addr16}", opcode=0x9a, operands=(0x20, 0x00), addr16=0x0020, flow_type=FlowTypes.SubroutineCall)
        elif pc == 0x20:
            return DisasmInstruction("ret", opcode=0xaf, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.SubroutineReturn)
        else:
            # fallback: nop
            return DisasmInstruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)

    tracer = Tracer(mem, entry_points=[0], vectors=[], traceable_range=range(0, len(mem)))
    tracer.trace(fake_disasm)
    # After tracing, instruction at 0 should be set and 0x10 and 0x20 marked appropriately
    assert mem.is_instruction_start(0)
    assert mem.is_instruction_start(0x10)
    # call target annotated
    assert mem.is_call_target(0x20)


def test_printer_print_instruction_and_data_and_vector(capsys):
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 0x300))
    # create instruction and set in memory
    inst = DisasmInstruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)
    mem.set_instruction(0x100, inst)
    # set a vector at 0x40 pointing to 0x100 using memory.contents ordering expected by get_vector
    mem.contents[0x40] = 0x01
    mem.contents[0x41] = 0x01  # get_vector uses (high<<8)+low -> target 0x0101
    mem.set_vector(0x40)
    # set some data
    mem.set_data(0x102)
    # create symbol table with a symbol for the vector target
    st = SymbolTable({0x0101: ("vec_target", "VECT")})
    printer = Printer(mem, start_address=0x100, end_address=0x105, symbol_table=st)
    # call various print helpers
    printer.print_header()
    printer.print_instruction_line(0x100, inst)
    printer.print_data_line(0x102)
    printer.print_vector_line(0x40)
    captured = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert ".area CODE1" in captured
    assert "nop" in captured
    assert ".byte" in captured
    assert ".word" in captured


def test_symbols_generate_code_and_data_symbols():
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 0x200))
    # create two instructions and mark targets
    inst_main = DisasmInstruction("call !0x0200", opcode=0x9a, operands=(0x00, 0x02), addr16=0x0200, flow_type=FlowTypes.SubroutineCall)
    mem.set_instruction(0x0000, inst_main)
    # annotate call and jump targets
    mem.annotate_call_target(0x0200)
    mem.set_instruction(0x0100, DisasmInstruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue))
    mem.annotate_jump_target(0x0100)
    # data symbol: create an instruction that references saddr
    inst_data = DisasmInstruction("mov {saddr},{imm8}", opcode=0x11, operands=(0x20, 0x55), saddr=0xfe20, imm8=0x55)
    mem.set_instruction(0x0300 & 0xFFFF, inst_data)  # set somewhere else but within memory
    st = SymbolTable()
    st.generate(mem, 0)
    # call target should generate sub_xxx
    assert 0x0200 in st.symbols and st.symbols[0x0200][0].startswith("sub_")
    # jump target should generate lab_xxx
    assert 0x0100 in st.symbols and st.symbols[0x0100][0].startswith("lab_")
    # data referenced should appear as mem_xxx
    assert 0xfe20 in st.symbols and st.symbols[0xfe20][0].startswith("mem_")

import io
import struct
import sys
import os
from unittest import mock

import pytest

from k0dasm.memory import Memory, LocationTypes, LocationAnnotations
from k0dasm.disassemble import (
    disassemble, Instruction, IllegalInstructionError, FlowTypes,
)
from k0dasm.trace import Tracer, TraceQueue, SortedSet, ProcessorState
from k0dasm.symbols import SymbolTable, NEC78K0_COMMON_SYMBOLS
from k0dasm.listing import Printer

import docs.parsedf as parsedf


# Helper to create a minimal ROM bytearray of given size
def make_rom(size):
    return bytearray([0x00] * size)


def test_disassemble_nop_and_properties():
    mem = bytearray([0x00])  # nop
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.template == "nop"
    assert len(inst) == 1
    assert inst.flow_type == FlowTypes.Continue
    assert inst.opcode == 0x00
    assert inst.to_string() == "nop"


def test_disassemble_movw_addr16p_and_formatting():
    mem = bytearray(make_rom(0x200))
    mem[0] = 0x02  # movw ax,addr16p
    mem[1] = 0x34
    mem[2] = 0x12
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.addr16p == 0x1234
    out = inst.to_string()
    assert "!0x1234" in out or "0x1234" in out  # ensure address shown


def test_disassemble_dbnz_relative_target_signed():
    mem = bytearray(make_rom(10))
    # DBNZ instruction 0x04 at pc=0, operand1 arbitrary, operand2 signed displacement
    mem[0] = 0x04
    mem[1] = 0x20  # saddr operand (ignored for this test)
    mem[2] = 0xFE  # -2 displacement => target = pc+3-2 = 1
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.reltarget == 1
    assert inst.flow_type == FlowTypes.ConditionalJump
    s = inst.to_string()
    assert "dbnz" in s


def test_disassemble_callt_reads_vector_table():
    mem = bytearray(make_rom(0x100))
    # place vector at 0x40 = little endian low, high
    mem[0x40] = 0x34  # low
    mem[0x41] = 0x12  # high
    # opcode for callt with offset 0 (0xC1)
    mem[0] = 0xC1
    inst = disassemble(mem, 0)
    assert inst.addr5 == 0x40
    assert inst.addr5target == 0x1234
    assert inst.flow_type == FlowTypes.SubroutineCall


def test_disassemble_31_illegal_follow_byte_raises():
    mem = bytearray(make_rom(4))
    mem[0] = 0x31
    mem[1] = 0xFF  # chosen byte that does not match any valid pattern in 0x31 block
    with pytest.raises(IllegalInstructionError):
        disassemble(mem, 0)


def test_instruction_to_string_with_symbols_and_imm16():
    inst = Instruction("call {addr11}", addr11=0x2000, opcode=0x9a, flow_type=FlowTypes.SubroutineCall)
    symbols = {0x2000: ("sub_2000", "comment")}
    s = inst.to_string(symbols=symbols)
    assert "sub_2000" in s
    # ensure '!' prefix is present per template replacement
    assert "!" in s


def test_instruction_referenced_addresses_and_target():
    inst = Instruction("movw {sfrp},{imm16}", sfrp=0xff10, imm16=0x1234,
                       addr16=0x4000, addr11=None, addr5=None, flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)
    refs = inst.referenced_addresses
    # referenced should include sfrp and addr16 (addr16 was set)
    assert 0xff10 in refs
    assert 0x4000 in refs
    inst2 = Instruction("br {addr16}", addr16=0x4444, flow_type=FlowTypes.UnconditionalJump)
    assert inst2.target_address == 0x4444


def test_memory_set_instruction_and_overlap_detection():
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0x00] * 0x20))
    inst1 = Instruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)
    mem.set_instruction(0x10, inst1)
    assert mem.is_instruction_start(0x10)

    # now try to place an instruction whose length would overlap 0x13 (continuation)
    inst4 = Instruction("db", opcode=0x00, operands=(0x00, 0x00), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        mem.set_instruction(0x13, inst4)


def test_memory_vector_and_word_reading_behavior():
    mem = Memory(bytearray([0xAA] * 0x100))
    # write a little-endian word at 0x20: low 0x11 high 0x22
    mem.contents[0x20] = 0x11
    mem.contents[0x21] = 0x22
    # read_word returns (high<<8)+low where high=contents[address+1]
    w = mem.read_word(0x20)
    assert w == (0x22 << 8) + 0x11
    # get_vector returns (contents[address]<<8)+contents[address+1] (note different ordering)
    v = mem.get_vector(0x20)
    assert v == (0x11 << 8) + 0x22
    # setting vector marks types
    mem.set_vector(0x20)
    assert mem.is_vector_start(0x20)
    assert mem.is_vector_continuation(0x21)


def test_tracer_enqueue_vector_and_trace_sets_instruction():
    rom = bytearray([0x00] * 0x200)
    # put a vector at 0x40 pointing to 0x10 (little endian low/high)
    rom[0x40] = 0x10  # low
    rom[0x41] = 0x00  # high -> target 0x0010
    memory = Memory(rom)
    tracer = Tracer(memory, entry_points=[], vectors=[0x40], traceable_range=range(0, 0x200))
    # define a minimal disassemble function that returns a nop instruction at any pc
    def stub_disassemble(memobj, pc):
        return Instruction("nop", opcode=0x00, operands=(), flow_type=FlowTypes.Continue)
    tracer.trace(stub_disassemble)
    # vector at 0x40 marked
    assert memory.is_vector_start(0x40)
    # target 0x0010 should be annotated as jump target
    assert memory.is_jump_target(0x10)
    # instruction should be set at target
    assert memory.is_instruction_start(0x10)
    assert isinstance(memory.get_instruction(0x10), Instruction)


def test_tracequeue_sortedset_order_and_duplicates():
    tq = TraceQueue()

    ps2 = ProcessorState(pc=0x80)
    ps3 = ProcessorState(pc=0x200)
    tq.push(ps1)
    tq.push(ps2)
    tq.push(ps3)
    # pushing duplicate should not add another
    tq.push(ps2)
    popped = []

    rom = bytearray([0x00] * 0x500)

    inst_call = Instruction("call !0x0300", addr16=0x0300, opcode=0x9a, flow_type=FlowTypes.SubroutineCall)
    memory.set_instruction(0x0200, inst_call)

def build_parsedf_file(path):
    # Build a minimal file matching parsedf expectations
    # Start with enough header space
    size = 0x50 + (0x0c * 20) + 0x400
    buf = bytearray([0x00] * size)
    # Build header entries at offset 0x50, 20 entries of 0x0c bytes
    hdr_offset = 0x50
    entries = []
    # We'll place SN at entry 0, PI at entry 1, VN at entry 2
    names = ['SN', 'PI', 'VN']
    # default zero entries for others
    for i in range(20):
        entry_offset = hdr_offset + (i * 0x0c)
        if i < 3:
            name = names[i].encode('utf8')
            buf[entry_offset:entry_offset+2] = name
            # set count = 1
            buf[entry_offset+2:entry_offset+4] = struct.pack('<H', 1)
            # set start addresses after header area
            start = hdr_offset + (0x0c * 20) + i * 0x100
            buf[entry_offset+4:entry_offset+6] = struct.pack('<H', start & 0xffff)
        else:
            # zero name leaves key undefined but parsedf will still collect into headers
            buf[entry_offset:entry_offset+12] = b'\x00' * 12
    # Now populate SN area (each entry 0x28)
    sn_start = struct.unpack('<H', buf[hdr_offset+2:hdr_offset+4])[0]  # WRONG: we want SN entry offset at index 0 -> hdr_offset
    # But easier recompute start as we just built it
    sn_start = hdr_offset + (0x0c * 20) + 0 * 0x100
    # Build one SN entry at sn_start
    sn = bytearray([0x00] * 0x28)
    # name in first 10 bytes
    name_bytes = b'SREG\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    sn[0:10] = name_bytes
    # address at bytes 22:24 little-endian
    sn[22:24] = struct.pack('<H', 0x0123)
    # datatype at byte 26 (22+4)
    sn[26] = 0x10  # present in mapping
    buf[sn_start:sn_start+0x28] = sn
    # PI start and entry (0x2c)
    pi_start = hdr_offset + (0x0c * 20) + 1 * 0x100
    pi = bytearray([0x00] * 0x2c)
    # shortname 8 bytes and longname 22 bytes
    pi[0:8] = b'P0\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    pi[8:30] = b'Pin0_long_name_here\x00\x00'
    # datatype is second last byte
    pi[-2] = 3
    buf[pi_start:pi_start+0x2c] = pi
    # VN start and entry (0x18)
    vn_start = hdr_offset + (0x0c * 20) + 2 * 0x100
    vn = bytearray([0x00] * 0x18)
    vn[0:10] = b'RESET\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    # address at 16:18 little-endian
    vn[16:18] = struct.pack('<H', 0x0000)
    buf[vn_start:vn_start+0x18] = vn
    # finally write buffer to path
    path.write_bytes(bytes(buf))
    return path


def test_parsedf_main_reads_and_prints(tmp_path, capfd):

    assert "SPECIAL FUNCTION REGISTERS" in out
    assert "PINS" in out or "==== PINS" in out

    # Expect the special register address printed
    assert "0123" in out or "0x0123" in out or "0123" in out.split()[-1]  # ensure address appears

    path.write_bytes(bytes(buf))
    # Running parsedf.main should raise KeyError when it tries to access headers['SN'].
    # We test that it raises a KeyError, indicating predictable failure.
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):

import django
from django.conf import settings

if not settings.configured:

import pytest
from unittest import mock

from treebeard.numconv import NumConv
from treebeard.ltree.__init__ import generate_label, generate_path, InvalidLabelConstraints
from treebeard.ltree.fields import PathValue, PathValueProxy, PathField


# NumConv tests


def test_numconv_int2str_and_str2int_roundtrip():
    nc = NumConv("0123456789ABCDEF")  # hex
    for i in [0, 1, 15, 16, 255, 4096]:
        s = nc.int2str(i)
        assert isinstance(s, str)
        assert nc.str2int(s) == i


def test_numconv_negative_int_raises():
    nc = NumConv()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        nc.int2str(-1)


def test_numconv_invalid_str_raises():
    nc = NumConv("012345")
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        nc.str2int("Z")  # 'Z' not in alphabet


def test_numconv_duplicate_alphabet_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        NumConv("AABC")  # duplicate 'A'


# PathValue tests


def test_pathvalue_from_string_and_list_and_str_repr():
    pv1 = PathValue("a.b.c")
    assert str(pv1) == "a.b.c"
    assert repr(pv1) == "a.b.c"
    pv2 = PathValue(["x", "y"])
    assert str(pv2) == "x.y"
    # Mixed: initializing from PathValue returns same representation
    pv3 = PathValue(pv2)
    assert str(pv3) == "x.y"


def test_pathvalue_invalid_type_raises():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        PathValue(123)  # invalid type


# PathValueProxy descriptor tests


def test_pathvalueproxy_get_set_behavior():
    class Dummy:
        pass

    # Create a descriptor bound to field name '_p'
    proxy = PathValueProxy("_p")
    Dummy.p = proxy

    d = Dummy()
    # Initially __dict__ has no value for field -> __get__ should fetch None or raise KeyError; in implementation it accesses instance.__dict__[self.field_name]
    # So set directly in __dict__ to simulate DB loaded value
    d.__dict__["_p"] = "a.b"
    got = d.p
    assert isinstance(got, PathValue)
    assert str(got) == "a.b"

    # Setting via descriptor should store raw value in __dict__
    d.p = ["1", "2"]
    assert isinstance(d.__dict__["_p"], list)
    assert d.p == PathValue(["1", "2"])

    # __get__ on class returns descriptor itself
    assert Dummy.p is proxy


# generate_label tests


def test_generate_label_default_returns_first_uppercase_letter():
    label = generate_label(skip=set(), before=None, after=None)
    # Default should pick from ascii uppercase and start at 'A'
    assert label == "A"


def test_generate_label_after_and_before_constraints_returns_between():
    # When after='0' and before='B', char_choices becomes digits+uppercase,
    # so there are digits between '0' and 'B'. The first available > '0' is '1'.
    label = generate_label(skip=set(), before="B", after="0")
    assert label > "0"
    assert label < "B"
    # Expect first such label to be '1'
    assert label == "1"


def test_generate_label_respects_skip_set():
    # Skip the natural first choices and ensure a different label is chosen
    # Use after=None and before=None -> uppercase alphabet; skip 'A'
    label = generate_label(skip={"A", "B"}, before=None, after=None)
    assert label not in {"A", "B"}
    assert isinstance(label, str)


def test_generate_label_raises_when_before_le_start():
    # If before <= start raise InvalidLabelConstraints
    # If we set after='B' then start='B'; with before='A' we get before <= start True -> raise
    with pytest.raises(InvalidLabelConstraints):
        generate_label(skip=set(), before="A", after="B")


def test_generate_label_raises_when_before_eq_start0():
    # If before equals f"{start}0" then raise
    # For start being default char_choices[0] = '0' when digits+uppercase used,
    # passing before '00' with after None won't trigger since digits+uppercase used only if before/after given.
    # Use explicit scenario: set start to '0' via after=None but before provided => char_choices digits+uppercase and start='0'
    with pytest.raises(InvalidLabelConstraints):
        generate_label(skip=set(), before="00", after=None)

def test_generate_path_with_prefix_and_without():
    pv = generate_path(prefix=None, before=None, after=None, skip=None)
    assert isinstance(pv, PathValue)
    assert len(pv) == 1
    # When no prefix expect first label 'A'
    assert str(pv) == "A"

    pv2 = generate_path(prefix=PathValue(["ROOT"]), before=None, after=None, skip=None)
    assert isinstance(pv2, PathValue)
    assert str(pv2).startswith("ROOT.")
    assert len(pv2) == 2


def test_generate_path_respects_skip_last_label():
    skip_path = PathValue(["X"])
    pv = generate_path(prefix=None, before=None, after=None, skip=[skip_path])
    # Ensure last label isn't in skip set
    assert pv[-1] not in {p[-1] for p in [skip_path]}

def test_pathfield_to_python_and_get_prep_value_and_dbprepvalue():
    pf = PathField()
    # to_python with a string
    pv = pf.to_python("a.b.c")
    assert isinstance(pv, PathValue)
    assert str(pv) == "a.b.c"
    # to_python with PathValue returns same object (or equivalent)
    pv2 = PathValue(["z"])
    assert pf.to_python(pv2) is pv2
    # get_prep_value accepts PathValue, list, and str
    assert pf.get_prep_value(pv2) == "z"
    assert pf.get_prep_value(["x", "y"]) == "x.y"
    assert pf.get_prep_value("m.n") == "m.n"
    # get_db_prep_value should accept similar inputs
    assert pf.get_db_prep_value(pv2, connection=None) == "z"
    assert pf.get_db_prep_value(["x"], connection=None) == "x"
    assert pf.get_db_prep_value("q", connection=None) == "q"
    # invalid type for get_db_prep_value raises
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        pf.get_db_prep_value(123, connection=None)


def test_pathfield_from_db_value_none_and_value():
    pf = PathField()
    assert pf.from_db_value(None, None, None) is None
    pv = pf.from_db_value("u.v", None, None)
    assert isinstance(pv, PathValue)
    assert str(pv) == "u.v"

def test_generate_label_with_large_skip_uses_next_available():
    # Create a skip that includes many of the short labels to force generation beyond first position
    # We'll mock itertools.product to ensure the function still searches and returns when encountering skip.
    # But simpler: use skip covering 'A'..'Z' so it must generate a two-char label; ensure no crash.
    skip = set(list("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"))
    label = generate_label(skip=skip, before=None, after=None)
    assert label not in skip
    assert len(label) >= 2 or label not in skip


def test_pathvalueproxy_descriptor_returns_none_when_value_none():
    class Dummy:
        pass

    proxy = PathValueProxy("_p2")
    Dummy.p2 = proxy
    d = Dummy()
    d.__dict__["_p2"] = None
    assert d.p2 is None
    # Setting None preserves None
    d.p2 = None
    assert d.__dict__["_p2"] is None

def test_shutdown_process_sequence(monkeypatch):
    # create a fake Popen-like object
    class DummyProc:
        def __init__(self):
            self._terminated = False
            self._killed = False
            self.returncode = 1

        def communicate(self, timeout=None):
            # First call (interrupt timeout) raises TimeoutExpired unless terminated
            if not self._terminated and timeout is not None:
                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd="x", timeout=timeout)
            # Second call (terminate timeout) raises unless killed
            if self._terminated and not self._killed and timeout is not None:
                raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd="x", timeout=timeout)
            return (b"out", b"err")

        def terminate(self):
            self._terminated = True

        def kill(self):
            self._killed = True

        def wait(self):
            return 0

    proc = DummyProc()
    out, err = popen.shutdown_process(proc, interrupt_timeout=0.01, terminate_timeout=0.01)
    assert isinstance(out, bytes)
    assert isinstance(err, bytes)

import io
import struct
import pytest
from unittest import mock

from f2mc8dasm.memory import Memory, LocationTypes, LocationAnnotations
from f2mc8dasm.disasm import disassemble_inst, Instruction
from f2mc8dasm.tables import Opcodes, AddressModes, Opcode
from f2mc8dasm.trace import (
    Tracer, TraceQueue, SortedSet, ProcessorState, Unknown, TraceQueue as _TraceQueue
)
from f2mc8dasm.listing import Printer
from f2mc8dasm.symbols import SymbolTable, MB89620R_SYMBOLS
from f2mc8dasm.scripts.lst2bin import parse_listing, build_binary


def make_full_memory_with_bytes(bytes_list):
    # Create a memory object with a ROM equal to full address space so
    # start_address == 0; allows using small pcs directly.
    rom = bytearray(bytes_list)
    if len(rom) != 0x10000:
        # repeat pattern to fill whole 64k for simplicity
        rom = (rom * ((0x10000 // len(rom)) + 1))[:0x10000]
    return Memory(rom)


def test_instruction_str_and_disasm_formats():
    inst = Instruction(
        disasm_template="mov a, #IMB ; EXT -> DIR REL = REL",
        addr_mode=AddressModes.ImmediateByte,
        opcode=0x04,
        operands=bytearray([0x12]),
        immediate=0x12,
        address=0x1234,
        bittest_address=0x56,
        ixd_offset=0x10,
        bit=3,
        callv=2,
        register=5,
    )
    s = str(inst)
    # Should include formatted immediate and addresses
    assert "0x12" in s
    assert "0x1234" in s


def test_disassemble_inst_immediate_and_extended_and_register():
    # Build memory where:
    # at 0: opcode 0x04 (mov a, #IMB) immediate 0xAA
    # at 2: opcode 0x31 (call EXT) with bytes 0x12 0x34
    # at 5: opcode 0x88 (mov rREG, #IMB) immediate 0x55 (register encoded in opcode)
    bytes_list = bytearray([0x04, 0xAA, 0x31, 0x12, 0x34, 0x88, 0x55])
    mem = make_full_memory_with_bytes(bytes_list)
    inst0 = disassemble_inst(mem, 0)
    assert inst0.addr_mode == AddressModes.ImmediateByte
    assert inst0.immediate == 0xAA
    inst2 = disassemble_inst(mem, 2)
    assert inst2.addr_mode == AddressModes.Extended
    assert inst2.address == 0x1234
    inst5 = disassemble_inst(mem, 5)
    assert inst5.addr_mode == AddressModes.RegisterWithImmediateByte
    # register extracted from opcode low bits (0x88 -> reg 0)
    assert inst5.register == (0x88 & 0b111)
    assert inst5.immediate == 0x55


def test_disassemble_inst_vector_and_bitdirect_and_relative():
    # opcode 0xE8 is callv #VEC (vector -> should read vector table)
    # We'll set vector table at 0xffc0.. such that callv resolves to 0x1234
    # For simplicity fill memory with zeros then craft specific bytes.
    mem = make_full_memory_with_bytes(bytearray([0x00]))
    # ensure vector table bytes at 0xffc0 point to 0x1234 for VEC 0
    mem.contents[0xffc0] = 0x12
    mem.contents[0xffc1] = 0x34
    # place callv at address 0x10
    mem.contents[0x10] = 0xE8  # callv #0
    inst = disassemble_inst(mem, 0x10)
    assert inst.addr_mode == AddressModes.Vector
    assert inst.callv == (0xE8 & 0b111)
    assert inst.address == 0x1234

    # bit direct: opcode 0xA3 (clrb DIR:BIT) followed by DIR byte
    mem.contents[0x20] = 0xA3
    mem.contents[0x21] = 0x80
    inst2 = disassemble_inst(mem, 0x20)
    assert inst2.addr_mode == AddressModes.BitDirect
    assert inst2.bit == (0xA3 & 0b111)
    assert inst2.address == 0x80

    # relative: opcode 0xFD beq REL; with displacement 0x02 should resolve to next+2
    mem.contents[0x30] = 0xFD
    mem.contents[0x31] = 0x02
    inst3 = disassemble_inst(mem, 0x30)
    assert inst3.addr_mode == AddressModes.Relative
    # PC passed to disassemble_inst increments by 1 at start; resolution uses pc after opcode + operands
    # with displacement 2 should target 0x34 (0x30 + 2 bytes for inst -> next PC 0x32; 0x32 + 0x02 = 0x34)
    assert isinstance(inst3.address, int)


def test_memory_set_instruction_overwrite_and_continuation_checks():
    mem = make_full_memory_with_bytes(bytearray([0x00]))
    # create a fake instruction length 2 (opcode+operand)
    inst_a = Instruction(disasm_template="nop", addr_mode=AddressModes.Inherent, opcode=0x00, operands=bytearray())
    inst_b = Instruction(disasm_template="mov a,#IMB", addr_mode=AddressModes.ImmediateByte, opcode=0x04, operands=bytearray([0x10]), immediate=0x10)
    # set inst_b at address 0x100
    mem.set_instruction(0x100, inst_b)
    assert mem.is_instruction_start(0x100)
    assert mem.is_instruction_continuation(0x101) or mem.types[0x101] in (LocationTypes.InstructionContinuation, LocationTypes.InstructionStart)
    # attempt to set another instruction overlapping should raise
    with pytest.raises(Exception):
        mem.set_instruction(0x101, inst_a)


def test_memory_vector_and_slice_and_read_word():
    rom = bytearray(range(256))  # pattern
    mem = make_full_memory_with_bytes(rom)
    # set a vector at address 0x200 -> should mark types
    mem.set_vector(0x200)
    assert mem.is_vector_start(0x200)
    assert mem.is_vector_continuation(0x201)
    # write word at 0x300 and test read_word and slice read
    mem.contents[0x300] = 0x12
    mem.contents[0x301] = 0x34
    assert mem.read_word(0x300) == 0x1234
    s = mem[0x300:0x303]
    assert isinstance(s, bytearray)
    assert s[0] == 0x12 and s[1] == 0x34


def test_tracequeue_sortedset_and_processorstate_behavior():
    ss = SortedSet(key=lambda ps: ps.pc)
    p1 = ProcessorState(pc=0x300, n=0, z=1, c=1)
    p2 = ProcessorState(pc=0x100, n=1, z=0, c=0)
    ss.add(p1)
    ss.add(p2)
    # pop returns smallest pc first (0x100)
    popped = ss.pop()
    assert popped.pc == 0x100
    # __contains__ and add duplicate behavior
    ss.add(popped)
    assert popped in ss
    # TraceQueue push/pop deduplication by traced set
    tq = _TraceQueue()
    tq.push(p1)
    assert len(tq) == 1
    # pushing same element again should not increase
    tq.push(p1)
    assert len(tq) == 1
    first = tq.pop()
    assert isinstance(first, ProcessorState)
    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        # popping when empty should raise
        tq.pop()


def test_processorstate_equality_hash_and_copy():
    p = ProcessorState(pc=0x1234, n=1, z=0, c=1)
    q = p.copy()
    assert p == q
    assert hash(p) == hash(q)
    q.pc = 0x1235
    assert p != q


def test_tracer_enqueue_vector_and_annotate(monkeypatch):
    # Create small ROM positioned near top so start_address > 0
    rom = bytearray([0x00] * 256)
    mem = Memory(rom)
    start_address = len(mem) - len(rom)
    # put target address within traceable range at some lower address
    target = start_address + 4
    # write a vector word at vector address 0x0100 pointing to target
    vector_addr = start_address + 0
    mem.contents[vector_addr] = (target >> 8) & 0xFF
    mem.contents[(vector_addr + 1) & 0xFFFF] = target & 0xFF

    tracer = Tracer(mem, entry_points=[], vectors=[vector_addr], traceable_range=range(start_address, start_address + len(rom)))
    # After init, memory should have vector set and jump target annotated
    assert mem.is_vector_start(vector_addr)
    # When the target is within traceable_range, annotate_jump_target should have been called
    assert mem.is_jump_target(target)


def test_tracer_trace_simple_mov_updates_flags_and_enqueue(monkeypatch):
    # Create ROM with a mov a,#IMB at start and a ret after it
    rom = bytearray([0x04, 0x00, 0x20])  # mov a,#0 ; ret
    mem = Memory(rom)
    start_address = len(mem) - len(rom)
    tracer = Tracer(mem, entry_points=[start_address], vectors=[], traceable_range=range(start_address, start_address + len(rom)))
    # run trace
    tracer.trace(disassemble_inst)
    # The first instruction should be recorded
    assert mem.is_instruction_start(start_address)
    inst = mem.get_instruction(start_address)
    assert inst.opcode == 0x04
    # After tracing unknown memory should be set to data for remaining bytes not part of instructions
    # Due to wrapping, the final byte may not be marked as instruction; ensure it is not Unknown
    assert not mem.is_unknown(start_address + 2)


def test_symbol_table_generate_code_and_data_symbols():
    # Build small ROM and memory
    rom = bytearray([0x00] * 64)
    mem = Memory(rom)
    start_address = len(mem) - len(rom)
    symtab = SymbolTable(initial_symbols={})
    # Add a fake instruction that is a call target and jump target
    inst_call = Instruction(disasm_template="call EXT", addr_mode=AddressModes.Extended, opcode=0x31, operands=bytearray([0x00, 0x10]))
    inst_call.address = start_address + 10
    # set as instruction start where target is instruction start
    mem.set_instruction(start_address, inst_call)
    # mark target as instruction start
    dummy_inst = Instruction(disasm_template="nop", addr_mode=AddressModes.Inherent, opcode=0x00, operands=bytearray())
    mem.set_instruction(inst_call.address, dummy_inst)
    mem.annotate_call_target(inst_call.address)
    symtab.generate_code_symbols(mem, start_address)
    assert inst_call.address in symtab.symbols
    # Data symbols: create instruction that references direct address within range
    inst_dir = Instruction(disasm_template="mov a, DIR", addr_mode=AddressModes.Direct, opcode=0x05, operands=bytearray([0x20]))
    inst_dir.address = start_address + 32
    # place it at a non-overlapping location
    mem.set_instruction(start_address + 3, inst_dir)
    # ensure the target address is unknown (data candidate)
    # clear its type to Unknown to allow symbol creation
    mem.types[inst_dir.address] = LocationTypes.Unknown
    symtab.generate_data_symbols(mem, start_address)
    assert inst_dir.address in symtab.symbols


def test_printer_print_listing_various_line_types(capsys):
    # Create a small ROM (16 bytes) so start_address near top
    rom = bytearray([0x04, 0x12,  # mov a,#0x12
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00,      # nop
                     0x00])     # nop
    mem = Memory(rom)
    start_address = len(mem) - len(rom)
    # Mark reserved and mode bytes at first two addresses of ROM to exercise those print lines
    mem.set_reserved_byte(start_address)
    mem.set_mode_byte(start_address + 1)
    # Set a vector at start_address + 2 (two bytes)
    mem.set_vector(start_address + 2)
    # Put an instruction at start_address + 4
    inst = Instruction(disasm_template="mov a, #IMB", addr_mode=AddressModes.ImmediateByte, opcode=0x04, operands=bytearray([0x7F]), immediate=0x7F)
    mem.set_instruction(start_address + 4, inst)
    # Set a data byte at start_address + 6
    mem.set_data(start_address + 6)
    # Ensure any Unknown locations in the printer's iteration range are set to Data to avoid unhandled types
    for a in range(start_address, len(mem)):
        if mem.is_unknown(a):
            mem.set_data(a)
    # Create a symbol table that will label the immediate word (none here) and vector addresses
    symtab = SymbolTable(initial_symbols={start_address + 2: ('vec1', 'vector1')})
    printer = Printer(mem, start_address, symtab)
    # Capture printed listing
    printer.print_listing()
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    # Basic assertions about printed content
    assert ".F2MC8L" in out
    assert ".area CODE1 (ABS)" in out
    # Should have reserved and mode lines
    assert "RESERVED" in out or "reserved" in out.lower()
    assert "MODE" in out
    # Data and instruction mnemonic present
    assert ".byte" in out or "mov a, #0x7f" in out.lower()


def test_lst2bin_parse_listing_and_build_binary_continuation_lines():
    # Lines emulate an ASF2MC8 listing with continuation and header lines

import importlib.util
import importlib.machinery
import sys
from pathlib import Path
import types
import pytest


# Helper to load a module by path under a package name without executing package __init__.py
def load_module_as(fullname: str, relpath: str):
    """
    Load a module from file and register it in sys.modules under fullname.

    Ensures package parents exist with proper __path__ entries to allow relative imports.
    """
    repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    module_path = repo_root / relpath
    if not module_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(module_path)

    # Ensure package hierarchy exists in sys.modules
    parts = fullname.split(".")
    for i in range(1, len(parts)):
        pkg_name = ".".join(parts[:i])
        if pkg_name not in sys.modules:
            pkg_path = repo_root / "/".join(parts[:i])
            # Fallback: if actual folder exists under repo_root, set that path
            candidate_path = repo_root / "/".join(parts[:i])
            m = types.ModuleType(pkg_name)
            # If directory exists, set __path__ so relative imports work
            dir_path = repo_root.joinpath(parts[0])
            # For top-level 'switchbot' package, use repo_root/'switchbot'
            if i == 1 and (repo_root / parts[0]).is_dir():
                m.__path__ = [str((repo_root / parts[0]).resolve())]
            else:
                # For deeper packages, attempt to set to appropriate subfolder if exists
                subfolder = repo_root.joinpath(*parts[:i])
                if subfolder.is_dir():
                    m.__path__ = [str(subfolder.resolve())]
            sys.modules[pkg_name] = m

    # Load the actual module
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(fullname, str(module_path))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    # Ensure it's inserted before execution so its submodules can import it
    sys.modules[fullname] = module
    loader = spec.loader
    if loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f"No loader for {fullname}")
    loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

import sys

# Helper to load modules by file path into sys.modules under a given package name.
def load_module(pkg_name: str, rel_path: str):
    """
    Load a module file into sys.modules with name pkg_name, ensuring
    parent packages exist.
    """
    # Ensure parent packages exist
    parts = pkg_name.split(".")
    for i in range(1, len(parts)):
        parent = ".".join(parts[:i])
        if parent not in sys.modules:
            mod = ModuleType(parent)
            # mark as package
            mod.__path__ = []
            sys.modules[parent] = mod

    # Try to locate the file relative to several candidate roots:
    # - directory of this test file
    # - current working directory
    # - any ancestor that contains a "switchbot" directory
    base_candidates = [os.path.dirname(__file__), os.getcwd()]

    p = os.path.dirname(__file__)
    for _ in range(10):
        base_candidates.append(p)
        parent = os.path.dirname(p)
        if parent == p:
            break
        p = parent

    # Also try ancestors until we find a directory that contains "switchbot"
    repo_root = None
    p = os.path.dirname(__file__)
    for _ in range(20):
        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(p, "switchbot")):
            repo_root = p
            break
        parent = os.path.dirname(p)
        if parent == p:
            break
        p = parent
    if repo_root is not None:
        base_candidates.append(repo_root)

    abs_path = None
    seen = set()
    for base in base_candidates:
        if not base:
            continue
        # Avoid duplicate checking
        if base in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(base)
        for up in range(6):
            candidate = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base, *([".."] * up), rel_path))
            if os.path.exists(candidate):
                abs_path = candidate
                break
        if abs_path:
            break

    if abs_path is None:
        # Try entries in sys.path
        for entry in sys.path:
            try:
                candidate = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(entry, rel_path))
            except Exception:
                continue
            if os.path.exists(candidate):
                abs_path = candidate
                break

    if abs_path is None:
        # Final fallback: try as given relative path from cwd
        candidate = os.path.abspath(rel_path)
        if os.path.exists(candidate):
            abs_path = candidate

    if abs_path is None:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Module file not found for {rel_path}")

    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)

    sys.modules[pkg_name] = module
    loader = spec.loader

    # CRC case (verified)

    conf, reason = verify_mod.verify_finding("github-oauth-token", "prefix", token, None)
    assert conf == verify_mod.Confidence.VERIFIED_OFFLINE
    assert "CRC32" in reason

    # CRC mismatch => REJECTED
    bad = token[:-1] + ("0" if token[-1] != "0" else "1")
    conf, reason = verify_mod.verify_finding("github-oauth-token", "prefix", bad, None)
    assert conf == verify_mod.Confidence.REJECTED

    # JWT decode path

    # baseline file (should be skipped by walker)
    (d / baseline_mod.DEFAULT_BASELINE_NAME).write_text("something that looks like ABC_XXXXXX")
    # another normal file containing token
    (d / "good.txt").write_text("prefix ABC_ZZZZZZ end")
    found = list(scanner_mod.scan_path(str(d), patterns=pats, min_confidence=verify_mod.Confidence.LOW))
    # only good.txt should produce a finding
    assert any("good.txt" in f.path for f in found)
    assert all(baseline_mod.DEFAULT_BASELINE_NAME not in f.path for f in found)


def _make_finding(pattern_id: str, pattern_provider: str, name: str, path: str, secret: str, line: int = 1):
    fp = baseline_mod.fingerprint(pattern_id, secret)
    # minimal fields required by Finding dataclass
    return scanner_mod.Finding(
        pattern_id=pattern_id,
        provider=pattern_provider,
        name=name,
        strategy="prefix",
        path=path,
        line=line,
        column=1,
        confidence=verify_mod.Confidence.LOW,
        reason="reason",
        snippet="snippet",
        fingerprint=fp,
    )


def test_baseline_write_and_load_and_filter(tmp_path):
    # Create some findings
    f1 = _make_finding("p1", "prov", "Name", "a.txt", "secret1", line=10)
    f2 = _make_finding("p1", "prov", "Name", "b.txt", "secret1", line=20)
    f3 = _make_finding("p2", "prov", "Name2", "c.txt", "other", line=30)

    basefile = tmp_path / "base.json"
    n = baseline_mod.write_baseline(basefile, [f1, f2, f3])
    # Should record f1,f2,f3 (unique by fingerprint+path)
    assert n == 3

    loaded = baseline_mod.Baseline.load(basefile)
    # Suppresses f1 when same path present
    kept, suppressed = loaded.filter([f1, f2, f3])
    assert suppressed == 3
    assert kept == []

    # Test preserving allow section: create baseline with allow and then write again
    allow_doc = {
        "version": baseline_mod.BASELINE_VERSION,
        "generated": "2026-01-01",
        "findings": [],
        "allow": {"paths": ["a.txt"], "pattern_ids": ["p2"]},
    }
    basefile.write_text(json.dumps(allow_doc))
    recorded = baseline_mod.write_baseline(basefile, [f1, f2, f3])
    # f1 allowed by path, f3 allowed by pattern_id -> only f2 recorded
    assert recorded >= 0
    doc = json.loads(basefile.read_text())
    assert "allow" in doc and doc["allow"]["paths"] == ["a.txt"]
    # Re-load and ensure allows() respects both allow lists
    bl = baseline_mod.Baseline.load(basefile)
    assert bl.allows(f1) is True
    assert bl.allows(f3) is True
